source.credit_line: P. C. Manuk and Miss G. M. Coles Bequest through Art Fund

cultural.vision_reason: This is a knotted wool bag face with the classic Turkmen gul medallion layout, asymmetrical open knot, and elongated octagonal guls typical of Central Asian tribal weaving — consistent with a "regional" (Central Asian) attribution.

physical.physical_description:
WARP: white wool; Z2S; 24 threads per inch (90 per dm).

WEFT:  brown wool; Z spun; unplied; 2 parallel threads per shoot; 2 shoots after each row of knots; 21 knots per inch (81 per dm).

PILE: wool; 8 colours: red, orange, dark green, dark blue, blue, pink, brown, white; asymmetrical knot open to the right and tied around 2 threads; 252 knots per sq. inch (3645 knots per sq. dm).

SIDE FINISH: 3 cords overcast with red wool.

END FINISH: Lower: cut.  Upper: plain weave with red and then white woollen weft, turned and stitched.  Red and green wool plait sewn along fold but bits missing.

DESIGN: Field: red ground with two bands of three stepped and hooked guls, one above the other.  In the centre of each, a pink and blue quartered hexagon within a larger rectangle framed alternately pink and red.  The rectangle is also quartered, with dark green bottom left and top right corners, and white in inner top left and inner lower right.  There is a central band with two lozenge arrangements of eight blue-outlined, small rectangles each containing a white star and framing a geometric, hooked motif outlined in brown.  Similar upper and lower bands are partially evident.

Main border: rectangles with contrasting star-like motif and separated (upper and lower) by narrow blocks of red and (sides) by multi-coloured bands.

Inner and outer borders: pink ground (lower parts have red ground) altnerating with white and red flowerheads outlined in dark green.

Upper border: row of blue, dark green, brown and white horns rise directly from the outer border.

Apron: pile 19 cms. in depth; diagonal row of alternating dark blue and dark green sprigs with white flowers - the dark blue infilled with red or orange and the dark green

deep.production:
Bequest, part of a very large general bequest by P.C. Manuk, Manchester Sq. London W1
one of a "pair of saddlebags (connected to 'juval').  Turcoman (Salor), 19th century.

cf/ A.A. Bogolynbov (ed. Thompson 1973) ill.40, Siawosch Azadi (1975) ill. 10.  See T72-1948 for details.
mentioned "Turkoman Rugs in the V & A", by R. Pinner & M. Franses (intro. by Donald King), analyses by L. Pinner.  Hali 1980, vol. 2, no.4, p.303, 305, 315.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Turkmen/Central Asian tribal bag face with a knotted-pile gul (octagon-like hexagon) design and elem border typical of Turkmen weaving, consistent with the "_regional" (Central Asian) attribution and woven textile category.

physical.physical_description:
Bag face: described as woven.  NB some repiling at lower centre and far right and left.

WARP: cream wool, some plying of cream and brown; Z2S; depressed; 29 threads per inch (116 per dm).

WEFT: light brown wool; Z spun, unplied; 2 parallel threads to each shoot and 2 shoots after each row of knots; 19 knots per inch (81 to the dm).

PILE: wool and silk; 10 colours: dark red, red, orange, dark green, dark blue, blue, light blue (silk), pink (silk), dark brown, cream; an asymmetrical knot open to the left and tied around 2 threads; 276 knots per sq. inchh (4698 per sq. dm).

SIDE FINISH: both sides have one cord oversewn in dark blue wool.

END FINISH: Lower: 2.5 cms. plain weave with red and then with cream weft turned and stitched into place.  Front 1 cm. covered by dark blue woollen braid, with pink silk Z-plied fine cord attached to braid and lying between the braid and the lowest row of knots.  Upper 2.5 cm. of plain weave with cream weft, turned and stitched into place after a single line of jufti knots in dark blue.  Over these knots is stitched a blue fringe of four threads knotted loosely over a double cord of dark brown wool.  To the right of the fringe is one, tightly plaited.  The maximum fringe length is 11.5 cms.).

DESIGN: Field: this has a cream ground, with two bands of 10 serrated leaves in pink, dark blue, red, dark green and with an angular contrasting curl in the centre.  The upper and lower pairs of leaves are joined by their stems which frame a central band of stepped hexagons, each containing a rosette.  Tiny, five-pronged comb motifs are scattered over the field.

Borders: the main border has a red ground with a linked band of small guls quartered in cream and dark blue and containing quartered diamonds, some in pink and blue silk.  The border's guard stripes are pink silk.

The inner and outer borders have a brown ground with white diamond flowerheads with pink silk centres alternating with Xs in various colours.

All the above borders are surrounded by a solid red border.  The lowest border has reciprocal band of dark blue/red horned motifs.  The uppermost border is a chequered band with a red/dark red ground and white diamonds with pink silk frames and centres.  This border has a white, zigzag guard stripe.

Date catalogued: 21.2.95
